newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-GOUGH DENIES IRELAND ANOTHER SURPRISE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GOUGH DENIES IRELAND ANOTHER SURPRISE.

text.p: England fast bowler Darren Gough destroyed Ireland's hopes of another one-day suprise when he bowled Yorkshire to a comprehensive win in the NatWest Trophy on Tuesday.
Ireland, shock winners over Middlesex in the Benson and Hedges tournament earlier in the season, looked to be on their way to another upset when they reduced Yorkshire to 55 for six.
But a belligerent 46 from Gough plus 83 from Peter Hartley and 63 from Craig White boosted the county side to 249.
Gough then tore through the Ireland batting with seven for for 27, including a hat-trick, as Ireland were dismissed for 55.
Warwickshire, the second most successful team in the history of the competition, were another county team in trouble as they were reduced to 25 for six by Norfolk.
But then England hopeful Ashley Giles hit 69 in a seventh-wicket partnership of 137 with Andy Moles (64) as Warwickshire recovered to 207.
Giles then took over his primary role of left-arm spinner to dismantle Norfolk, taking five for 21 as they were bowled out for 127.
Holders Lancashire had an easier passage to the second round despite losing both of their England batsmen Mike Atherton and John Crawley cheaply against Berkshire.
Atherton was out for eight and Crawley 11, but then Graham Lloyd (96) and Mark Harvey (86) aided Lancashire to 351 for seven.
Berkshire survived their 60 overs but found runs hard to come by and finished on 182 for five.
